Concepts Relating to Adverse Consequences of Noise. Noise is 2. objectionable for commonsense reasons because it destroys the serenity of one's environment. Beyond that there are a number of specific concepts or ideas relating to noise. Current research efforts are directed toward establishing firm findings about certain noise phenomena and their consequences. 
a. General Hearing Loss or Damage. High intensity noises even of relatively short duration such as blasts or explosions are known to have destroyed or severely limited the hearing sense. Moreover, highly amplified rock-and-roll music, sports shooting, and other recreational uses might produce sound levels capable of producing hearing loss especially if exposures are prolonged or recurrent. Continuing exposures to levels exceeding 100dB(A) lead to temporary and, eventually, to permanent hearing loss.
